Lusitânia (basketball)|Lusitânia EXPERT]] | years10 = 2024 | team10 = Piratas de Los Lagos | years11 = 2024–2025 | team11 = [[KW Titans]] | years12 = 2025 | team12 = [[Tijuana Zonkeys]] | highlights = * [[Patriot League Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Patriot League Player of the Year]] (2021) * 2× First-team All-[[Patriot League]] (2020, 2021) * Second-team All-Patriot League (2019) * Patriot League All-Rookie Team (2018) * 2× [[Patriot League men's basketball tournament|Patriot League tournament]] MVP ([[2019 Patriot League men's basketball tournament|2019]], [[2021 Patriot League men's basketball tournament|2021]]) }} '''Jordan Kennedy Burns''' (born August 28, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Tijuana Zonkeys]] of the [[Circuito de Baloncesto de la Costa del Pacífico|CIBACOPA]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Colgate Raiders men's basketball|Colgate Raiders]]. ==High school career== Burns was a four-year [[basketball]] captain for [[John Marshall High School (Leon Valley, Texas)|John Marshall High School]] in [[San Antonio, Texas]]. Entering his freshman season, he stood {{convert|5|ft|7|in}} and weighed {{convert|110|lbs}}.{{cite web |last1=Hinojosa |first1=David |title=Burns' inner-drive takes him to the Big Dance |url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/high-school/article/Burns-inner-drive-takes-him-to-the-Big-Dance-13703687.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=April 27, 2020 |date=March 20, 2019}} Burns earned All-District honors in each season. As a senior, he led his team to the Conference 6A Region IV playoffs for its first time in 20 years and was named to the All-Region team. After initially committing to [[NCAA Division II]] program [[Midwestern State University|Midwestern State]], he switched his commitment to [[Colgate Raiders men's basketball|Colgate]], his only [[NCAA Division I]] offer.{{cite web |last1=Bailey |first1=Stephen |title=Colgate basketball PG Jordan Burns personifies program's underdog identity |url=https://www.syracuse.com/sports/2019/03/colgate-basketball-pg-jordan-burns-personifies-programs-underdog-identity.html |website=[[The Post-Standard]] |access-date=April 27, 2020 |date=March 18, 2019}}{{cite web |last1=Edelman |first1=KJ |title=Jordan Burns' decision to decommit lead him to become Colgate's second leading scorer |url=http://dailyorange.com/2017/12/jordan-burns-decision-decommit-lead-become-colgates-second-leading-scorer/ |website=[[The Daily Orange]] |access-date=April 27, 2020 |date=December 7, 2017}} To meet Colgate's academic requirements, Burns attended [[Kent School]] in [[Kent, Connecticut]], for a prep year. He averaged 19 points, five rebounds and four assists per game, leading Kent to the [[Founders League]] title while sharing league [[most valuable player]] (MVP) honors. ==College career== On November 19, 2017, in his third game for Colgate, Burns scored 26 points and shot 12-of-15 from the field in a 93–88 win over [[UMBC Retrievers men's basketball|UMBC]].{{cite web |title=Freshman Burns scores season-best 26, Colgate beats UMBC |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2017/11/19/freshman-burns-scores-season-best-26-colgate-beats-umbc/107855150/ |website=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=May 30, 2020 |date=November 19, 2017}} He was subsequently named [[Patriot League]] Rookie of the Week.{{cite web |title=Jordan Burns |url=https://gocolgateraiders.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jordan-burns/11211 |publisher=Colgate University Athletics |access-date=May 30, 2020}} On January 27, he scored a freshman season-high 27 points in an 83–69 victory over [[American Eagles men's basketball|American]].{{cite web |last1=Vielhauer |first1=Chelsea |title=Raiders Complete First-Ever Sweep Of American With 83–69 Win |url=https://gocolgateraiders.com/news/2018/1/27/mens-basketball-raiders-complete-first-ever-sweep-of-american-with-83-69-win.aspx |publisher=Colgate University Athletics |access-date=May 30, 2020 |date=January 27, 2018}} Burns subsequently earned Patriot League Rookie of the Week honors for a third time. As a freshman, he averaged 11.9 points, 2.9 assists and 2.7 rebounds per game, making the Patriot League All-Rookie Team.{{cite web |title=Men's Basketball 2017-18 All-Patriot League Teams and Major Awards Announced (2.26.18) |url=https://patriotleague.org/news/2018/2/26/mens-basketball-2017-18-all-patriot-league-teams-and-major-awards-announced-2-26-18.aspx?path=mbball |publisher=[[Patriot League]] |access-date=May 30, 2020 |date=February 26, 2018}} In the second game as a sophomore, on November 9, 2018, Burns recorded 30 points, six assists and five rebounds in an 87–74 win over [[Monmouth Hawks men's basketball|Monmouth]].{{cite web |title=Burns scores 30 as Colgate cruises past Monmouth 87–74 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401086013 |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=May 31, 2020 |date=November 9, 2018}} Four days later, he was named Patriot League Player of the Week.{{cite web |title=Patriot League Men's Basketball Players of the Week Announced (11.12.18) |url=https://patriotleague.org/news/2018/11/12/patriot-league-mens-basketball-players-of-the-week-announced-11-12-18.aspx |publisher=[[Patriot League]] |access-date=May 31, 2020 |date=November 12, 2018}} On March 13, 2019, Burns scored a sophomore season-high 35 points to go with six assists and three steals, leading his team to a 94–80 victory over [[Bucknell Bison men's basketball|Bucknell]] in the [[2019 Patriot League men's basketball tournament|2019 Patriot League tournament]] final. He was named tournament MVP and helped Colgate earn its first [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] berth since 1996. In the first round of the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2019 NCAA tournament]], Burns scored 32 points and made a career-high eight three-pointers in a 77–70 loss to second-seeded [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]].{{cite web |last1=McKee |first1=Ben |title=Colgate's Jordan Burns Shines, but Vols Find Way to Advance |url=https://www.rockytopinsider.com/2019/03/22/colgates-jordan-burns-shines-but-vols-find-way-to-advance/ |publisher=Rocky Top Insider |access-date=May 31, 2020 |date=March 22, 2019}} As a sophomore, he averaged 16.3 points, 5.7 assists and three rebounds per game and was named to the second team All-Patriot League. On November 26, 2019, in his junior season, Burns scored a career-high 40 points and made eight three-pointers in a 99–81 win over [[Green Bay Phoenix men's basketball|Green Bay]] at the [[Legends Classic (basketball tournament)|Legends Classic]] and was named tournament MVP. He recorded the most single-game points by a Colgate player since Tucker Neale in 1995 and surpassed the tournament scoring record.{{cite web |last1=Doroshenko |first1=Jordan |title=Burns Drops 40 Points in Win Over Green Bay |url=https://gocolgateraiders.com/news/2019/11/26/mens-basketball-burns-drops-40-points-in-win-over-green-bay.aspx |publisher=Colgate University Athletics |access-date=May 31, 2020 |date=November 26, 2019}} The performance helped him win Patriot League Player of the Week and Lou Henson National Player of the Week recognition on December 2.{{cite web |title=Patriot League Men's Basketball Players of the Week Announced (12.2.19) |url=https://patriotleague.org/news/2019/12/2/patriot-league-mens-basketball-players-of-the-week-announced-12-2-19.aspx
